review_notes: I read all 154 lines of the target and inspected the definitions and simp lemmas in Circle.lean, AddCircle/Real.lean, AddChar.lean, ZMod/Basic.lean, RootsOfUnity/Basic.lean, and the downstream uses in NumberTheory/LSeries/ZMod.lean and Analysis/Fourier/ZMod.lean. I did not execute Lean, so the proposed attributes and replacement lemmas are untested. I considered the specialized `rootsOfUnityCircleEquiv_comp_rootsOfUnityAddChar_val` formula but did not flag it as a missing simp rule because its right-hand side explicitly uses `ZMod.val` and the file treats such formulas as user-directed rather than global simp normal forms.

findings.excerpt: lemma stdAddChar_apply (j : ZMod N) : stdAddChar j = ↑(toCircle j) := rfl
findings.problem: This is the definitional evaluation lemma for `stdAddChar`, but it is not in the simp set. The analogous wrapper-removal lemma `rootsOfUnityAddChar_val` is tagged `@[simp]`, while downstream files have to put `stdAddChar_apply` explicitly into `simp only` sets. As written, ordinary `simp` has no rule for normalizing `stdAddChar j` to its underlying circle expression `↑(toCircle j)`.
findings.proposed_change: Attach `@[simp]` to `stdAddChar_apply`, or use `attribute [simp] stdAddChar_apply`. Keep the specialized `stdAddChar_coe` formula separate; if both are later made simp, also expose the `toCircle_intCast` step so the routes finish at the same exponential normal form.
findings.benefit: Ordinary `simp` would reduce `stdAddChar j` to the canonical underlying circle coercion, matching the existing `rootsOfUnityAddChar_val` interface and removing repeated manual inclusions from downstream simp sets.

evidence.excerpt:
@[simp] lemma rootsOfUnityAddChar_val (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (x : ZMod n) :
    (rootsOfUnityAddChar n x).val = toCircle x := by

findings.excerpt:
lemma toCircle_intCast (j : ℤ) :
    toCircle (j : ZMod N) = exp (2 * π * I * j / N) := by
findings.problem: The explicit formula lemmas for `ZMod.toCircle` at integer and natural casts are not `simp` lemmas. Consequently, even after the existing tagged rules reduce a root-of-unity character value to `toCircle x`, or after `stdAddChar_apply` would reduce it to `↑(toCircle j)`, `simp` has no rule to reach the advertised `Complex.exp` formula. The file itself has to use the reverse of `toCircle_natCast` at line 143 and the forward lemma at line 148, and LSeries/ZMod.lean calls `ZMod.toCircle_intCast` manually at line 162. The docstring explicitly recommends `toCircle_intCast` over the `ZMod.val`-based `toCircle_apply`, but this recommended formula is not exposed to `simp`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `toCircle_intCast` and its natural-cast specialization `toCircle_natCast` as `[simp]`. Leave `toCircle_apply` and `toCircle_eq_circleExp` untagged, since the former is explicitly described as `ZMod.val`-based and the latter is an alternate Circle-valued formula. The right-hand side `Complex.exp ...` is a terminal formula in this file: no existing lemma rewrites it back to `toCircle`, so this direction does not by itself introduce a cycle; I have not run Lean to verify termination.
findings.benefit: This completes the chain `stdAddChar`/`rootsOfUnityAddChar` -> `toCircle` -> `Complex.exp` for integer and natural casts, so `simp` can evaluate the standard character without repeating `toCircle_intCast`/`toCircle_natCast` in every proof. It also matches the file's own recommendation to lift arguments to `ℤ` and use the non-`val` formula.

evidence.excerpt:
Explicit formula for `toCircle j`. Note that this is "evil" because it uses `ZMod.val`. Where
possible, it is recommended to lift `j` to `ℤ` and use `toCircle_intCast` instead.

findings.excerpt:
lemma injective_toCircle : Injective (toCircle : ZMod N → Circle) :=
  (AddCircle.injective_toCircle one_ne_zero).comp (toAddCircle_injective N)
findings.problem: Injectivity is exposed only as an `Injective` theorem, not as a canonical `[simp]` iff lemma for equalities of character values. The related `ZMod.toAddCircle` API exposes `@[simp] toAddCircle_inj` and `@[simp] toAddCircle_eq_zero`. In this file, proofs must explicitly invoke `injective_stdAddChar.eq_iff` at line 98 and `ZMod.injective_toCircle.eq_iff` at line 152, so the simplifier has no direct rule reducing `toCircle j = toCircle k` or `stdAddChar j = stdAddChar k` to `j = k`.
findings.proposed_change:
Add canonical simp lemmas, for example:

@[simp] lemma toCircle_inj {j k : ZMod N} : toCircle j = toCircle k ↔ j = k := injective_toCircle.eq_iff
@[simp] lemma stdAddChar_inj {j k : ZMod N} : stdAddChar j = stdAddChar k ↔ j = k := injective_stdAddChar.eq_iff

Optionally add the corresponding equality-to-one forms using `AddChar.map_zero_eq_one`, about `toCircle j = 1 ↔ j = 0` and `stdAddChar j = 1 ↔ j = 0`.
findings.benefit: The simplifier could reduce character equalities to equalities of residues, the primitivity and bijectivity proofs would no longer need explicit `.eq_iff` rewrites, and the interface would match the existing `toAddCircle_inj`/`toAddCircle_eq_zero` API.

evidence.excerpt:
@[simp] lemma toAddCircle_inj {j k : ZMod N} : toAddCircle j = toAddCircle k ↔ j = k :=
  (toAddCircle_injective N).eq_iff

@[simp] lemma toAddCircle_eq_zero {j : ZMod N} : toAddCircle j = 0 ↔ j = 0 :=
  map_eq_zero_iff _ (toAddCircle_injective N)
